function.name: find_movie_showing
function.description: Find local movie theatres and their schedule for a specific movie Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. San Diego, CA

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find two movie theaters near San Diego that show Tenet at 5pm and No Time To Die at 7:30pm. We need to use the function find_movie_showing. Provide location: "San Diego, CA". movie: "Tenet" or "No Time To Die"? The function signature expects movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[]? Actually it's an array of movies? It says movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], time: string[]. So we can pass both movies and times. But the user wants two separate theaters: one showing Tenet at 5pm, another showing No Time To Die at 7:30pm. We could call the function twice: once for Tenet at 5pm, once for No Time To Die at 7:30pm. Or we could pass both movies and times arrays. But the function likely returns theaters that match all criteria. If we pass both movies and times, it might return theaters that show both movies at those times. That might not exist. So better to call twice.

Thus we will call find_movie_showing with location "San Diego, CA", movie "Tenet", time ["17:00"] (or "5:00 PM"). Then call again with movie "No Time To Die", time ["19:30"]. We'll then format the results.

We need to output the function calls. According to instruction, we should only output the function calls. So we produce two calls.
